sanskrit: draupadeyā raṇe kruddhā duryodhanam avārayan ekaikas tribhir ānarchat putraṃ tava viśāṃ pate
english: The sons of Draupadī, enraged in battle, held Duryodhana at bay; each one of them, O lord of the people, struck your son with three arrows.

sanskrit: putro 'pi tava durdharṣo draupadyās tanayān raṇe sāyakair niśitai rājann ājaghāna pṛthak pṛthak
english: And your unassailable son too, O king, smote the sons of Draupadī in battle, each one separately, with sharp shafts.

sanskrit: taiś cāpi viddhaḥ śuśubhe rudhireṇa samukṣitaḥ giriprasravaṇair yadvad girir dhātuvimiśritaiḥ
english: Pierced by them in turn and drenched with blood, he shone like a mountain streaked with mineral-laden torrents pouring down its slopes.

sanskrit: bhīṣmo 'pi samare rājan pāṇḍavānām anīkinīm kālayām āsa balavān pālaḥ paśugaṇān iva
english: Bhīṣma too, mighty in the fray, O king, drove back the host of the Pāṇḍavas as a herdsman drives the cattle of his flock.

sanskrit: tato gāṇḍīvanirghoṣaḥ prādurāsīd viśāṃ pate dakṣiṇena varūthinyāḥ pārthasyārīn vinighnataḥ
english: Then, O lord of the people, the twang of the Gāṇḍīva arose on the right of the army, as Pārtha struck down his foes.

sanskrit: uttasthuḥ samare tatra kabandhāni samantataḥ kurūṇāṃ cāpi sainyeṣu pāṇḍavānāṃ ca bhārata
english: On every side in that battle headless trunks rose up, O Bhārata, amid the armies of both the Kurus and the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: śoṇitodaṃ rathāvartaṃ gajadvīpaṃ hayormiṇam rathanaubhir naravyāghrāḥ prateruḥ sainyasāgaram
english: With chariots for boats those tigers among men crossed that sea of armies, whose water was blood, whose whirlpools were chariots, whose islands were elephants, and whose waves were horses.

sanskrit: chinnahastā vikavacā videhāś ca narottamāḥ patitās tatra dṛśyante śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ
english: With hands lopped off, stripped of armor, robbed of their bodies, the foremost of men were seen lying fallen there by hundreds and by thousands.

sanskrit: nihatair mattamātaṅgaiḥ śoṇitaughapariplutaiḥ bhūr bhāti bharataśreṣṭha parvatair ācitā yathā
english: With slain rutting elephants, awash in floods of blood, the earth shone, O best of the Bharatas, as though strewn with mountains.

sanskrit: tatrādbhutam apaśyāma tava teṣāṃ ca bhārata na tatrāsīt pumān kaś cid yo yoddhuṃ nābhikāṅkṣati
english: There we beheld a wondrous thing, O Bhārata, among both your men and theirs: there was not a single man there who did not yearn to fight.

sanskrit: evaṃ yuyudhire vīrāḥ prārthayānā mahad yaśaḥ tāvakāḥ pāṇḍavaiḥ sārdhaṃ kāṅkṣamāṇā jayaṃ yudhi
english: Thus the heroes fought, your warriors together with the Pāṇḍavas, seeking great renown and longing for victory in the battle.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tato duryodhano rājā lohitāyati bhāskare saṃgrāmarabhaso bhīmaṃ hantukāmo 'bhyadhāvata
english: Saṃjaya said: Then, as the sun reddened toward setting, King Duryodhana, frenzied with the battle and eager to slay Bhīma, charged upon him.

sanskrit: tam āyāntam abhiprekṣya nṛvīraṃ dṛḍhavairiṇam bhīmasenaḥ susaṃkruddha idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Beholding that hero among men, his inveterate foe, coming on, Bhīmasena, sorely enraged, spoke these words:

sanskrit: ayaṃ sa kālaḥ saṃprāpto varṣapūgābhikāṅkṣitaḥ adya tvāṃ nihaniṣyāmi yadi notsṛjase raṇam
english: This is the hour I have awaited through many a long year. Today I shall slay you, unless you forsake the field of battle.

sanskrit: adya kuntyāḥ parikleśaṃ vanavāsaṃ ca kṛtsnaśaḥ draupadyāś ca parikleśaṃ praṇotsyāmi hate tvayi
english: Today, with your death, I shall wipe out the affliction of Kuntī, the whole of our exile in the forest, and the affliction of Draupadī.

sanskrit: yat tvaṃ durodaro bhūtvā pāṇḍavān avamanyase tasya pāpasya gāndhāre paśya vyasanam āgatam
english: You who, turning gambler, held the Pāṇḍavas in contempt—behold now, O son of Gāndhārī, the calamity come upon you for that sin.

sanskrit: karṇasya matam ājñāya saubalasya ca yat purā acintya pāṇḍavān kāmād yatheṣṭaṃ kṛtavān asi
english: Following of old the counsel of Karṇa and of the son of Subala, you scorned the Pāṇḍavas and out of willfulness wrought your pleasure upon them.

sanskrit: yācamānaṃ ca yan mohād dāśārham avamanyase ulūkasya samādeśaṃ yad dadāsi ca hṛṣṭavat
english: And in your folly you spurned the Dāśārha when he came pleading, and gladly you gave Ulūka your insolent message.

sanskrit: adya tvā nihaniṣyāmi sānubandhaṃ sabāndhavam samīkariṣye tat pāpaṃ yat purā kṛtavān asi
english: Today I shall slay you with your followers and your kinsmen, and so wipe clean the sin you wrought of old.

sanskrit: evam uktvā dhanur ghoraṃ vikṛṣyodbhrāmya cāsakṛt samādāya śarān ghorān mahāśanisamaprabhān
english: Having spoken thus, he drew his dreadful bow and brandished it again and again, and took up terrible shafts that gleamed like the great thunderbolt.

sanskrit: ṣaḍviṃśat tarasā kruddho mumocāśu suyodhane jvalitāgniśikhākārān vajrakalpān ajihmagān
english: Swiftly, in fury, he loosed at once at Suyodhana twenty-six arrows, shaped like blazing tongues of fire, like thunderbolts, flying straight.

sanskrit: tato 'sya kārmukaṃ dvābhyāṃ sūtaṃ dvābhyāṃ ca vivyadhe caturbhir aśvāñ javanān anayad yamasādanam
english: With two he split his bow, with two he pierced his charioteer, and with four he sent his swift horses to the abode of Yama.

sanskrit: dvābhyāṃ ca suvikṛṣṭābhyāṃ śarābhyām arimardanaḥ chatraṃ ciccheda samare rājñas tasya rathottamāt
english: And with two well-drawn shafts that crusher of foes severed in the battle the royal parasol from the king's splendid chariot.

sanskrit: tribhiś ca tasya ciccheda jvalantaṃ dhvajam uttamam chittvā taṃ ca nanādoccais tava putrasya paśyataḥ
english: And with three he clove asunder his blazing, lofty standard; and having cut it down, he roared aloud before the very eyes of your son.

sanskrit: rathāc ca sa dhvajaḥ śrīmān nānāratnavibhūṣitaḥ papāta sahasā bhūmiṃ vidyuj jaladharād iva
english: And that splendid standard, adorned with many gems, fell suddenly from the chariot to the earth, like lightning from a storm-cloud.

sanskrit: jvalantaṃ sūryasaṃkāśaṃ nāgaṃ maṇimayaṃ śubham dhvajaṃ kurupateś chinnaṃ dadṛśuḥ sarvapārthivāḥ
english: All the kings saw the standard of the Kuru lord—the gleaming, jewel-wrought, splendid serpent emblem, bright as the sun—cut down.

sanskrit: athainaṃ daśabhir bāṇais tottrair iva mahāgajam ājaghāna raṇe bhīmaḥ smayann iva mahārathaḥ
english: Then Bhīma, that great car-warrior, smiling as it were, struck him in the fight with ten arrows, as one goads a great elephant with hooks.

sanskrit: tatas tu rājā sindhūnāṃ rathaśreṣṭho jayadrathaḥ duryodhanasya jagrāha pārṣṇiṃ satpuruṣocitām
english: Then Jayadratha, king of the Sindhus, foremost of car-warriors, guarded Duryodhana's rear as befits a man of worth.

sanskrit: kṛpaś ca rathināṃ śreṣṭhaḥ kauravyam amitaujasam āropayad rathaṃ rājan duryodhanam amarṣaṇam
english: And Kṛpa, foremost of car-warriors, mounted the wrathful Duryodhana of immeasurable might, that scion of the Kurus, upon his own chariot, O king.

sanskrit: sa gāḍhaviddho vyathito bhīmasenena saṃyuge niṣasāda rathopasthe rājā duryodhanas tadā
english: Sorely wounded and stricken by Bhīmasena in the encounter, King Duryodhana then sank down upon the floor of the chariot.

sanskrit: parivārya tato bhīmaṃ hantukāmo jayadrathaḥ rathair anekasāhasrair bhīmasyāvārayad diśaḥ
english: Then Jayadratha, eager to slay Bhīma, surrounded him and, with many thousands of chariots, barred every quarter against him.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭaketus tato rājann abhimanyuś ca vīryavān kekayā draupadeyāś ca tava putrān ayodhayan
english: Then, O king, Dhṛṣṭaketu and the valiant Abhimanyu, the Kekayas and the sons of Draupadī, did battle against your sons.

sanskrit: citrasenaḥ sucitraś ca citrāśvaś citradarśanaḥ cārucitraḥ sucāruś ca tathā nandopanandakau
english: Citrasena and Sucitra, Citrāśva and Citradarśana, Cārucitra and Sucāru, and likewise Nanda and Upananda—

sanskrit: aṣṭāv ete maheṣvāsāḥ sukumārā yaśasvinaḥ abhimanyurathaṃ rājan samantāt paryavārayan
english: these eight great archers, tender of years and full of glory, hemmed in the chariot of Abhimanyu on every side, O king.

sanskrit: ājaghāna tatas tūrṇam abhimanyur mahāmanāḥ ekaikaṃ pañcabhir viddhvā śaraiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ vajramṛtyupratīkāśair vicitrāyudhaniḥsṛtaiḥ
english: Then high-souled Abhimanyu swiftly smote them, piercing each one with five smooth-jointed arrows, shafts like the thunderbolt and like death itself, sped from his wondrous weapon.

sanskrit: amṛṣyamāṇās te sarve saubhadraṃ rathasattamam vavarṣur mārgaṇais tīkṣṇair giriṃ merum ivāmbudāḥ
english: Brooking it not, they all rained sharp arrows upon the son of Subhadrā, that best of car-warriors, as rain-clouds pour upon Mount Meru.

sanskrit: sa pīḍyamānaḥ samare kṛtāstro yuddhadurmadaḥ abhimanyur mahārāja tāvakān samakampayat yathā devāsure yuddhe vajrapāṇir mahāsurān
english: Though hard pressed in the battle, Abhimanyu, master of weapons and frenzied for the fight, made your warriors tremble, O great king, as the Wielder of the Thunderbolt made the great Asuras tremble in the war of gods and demons.

sanskrit: vikarṇasya tato bhallān preṣayām āsa bhārata caturdaśa rathaśreṣṭho ghorān āśīviṣopamān dhvajaṃ sūtaṃ hayāṃś cāsya chittvā nṛtyann ivāhave
english: Then, O Bhārata, that foremost of car-warriors sent against Vikarṇa fourteen terrible broad-headed shafts, like venomous serpents, cutting down his standard, his charioteer, and his horses, as though dancing in the battle.

sanskrit: punaś cānyāñ śarān pītān akuṇṭhāgrāñ śilāśitān preṣayām āsa saubhadro vikarṇāya mahābalaḥ
english: And again the mighty son of Subhadrā sent against Vikarṇa other arrows, yellow, with unblunted points, whetted on stone.

sanskrit: te vikarṇaṃ samāsādya kaṅkabarhiṇavāsasaḥ bhittvā dehaṃ gatā bhūmiṃ jvalanta iva pannagāḥ
english: Reaching Vikarṇa, those shafts fledged with heron and peacock feathers pierced his body and entered the earth, like blazing serpents.

sanskrit: te śarā hemapuṅkhāgrā vyadṛśyanta mahītale vikarṇarudhiraklinnā vamanta iva śoṇitam
english: Those arrows, gold-feathered and gold-pointed, drenched in Vikarṇa's blood, were seen upon the earth as though vomiting gore.

sanskrit: vikarṇaṃ vīkṣya nirbhinnaṃ tasyaivānye sahodarāḥ abhyadravanta samare saubhadrapramukhān rathān
english: Seeing Vikarṇa thus pierced through, his other brothers rushed in the battle upon the car-warriors led by the son of Subhadrā.

sanskrit: abhiyātvā tathaivāśu rathasthān sūryavarcasaḥ avidhyan samare 'nyonyaṃ saṃrabdhā yuddhadurmadāḥ
english: Charging swiftly likewise, those warriors splendid as the sun, mounted on their chariots, furious and frenzied for the fight, pierced one another in the battle.

sanskrit: durmukhaḥ śrutakarmāṇaṃ viddhvā saptabhir āśugaiḥ dhvajam ekena ciccheda sārathiṃ cāsya saptabhiḥ
english: Durmukha, having pierced Śrutakarman with seven swift arrows, severed his standard with one and his charioteer with seven.

sanskrit: aśvāñ jāmbūnadair jālaiḥ pracchannān vātaraṃhasaḥ jaghāna ṣaḍbhir āsādya sārathiṃ cābhyapātayat
english: His horses, swift as the wind, caparisoned in nets of gold, he reached and slew with six shafts, and struck down his charioteer.

sanskrit: sa hatāśve rathe tiṣṭhañ śrutakarmā mahārathaḥ śaktiṃ cikṣepa saṃkruddho maholkāṃ jvalitām iva
english: Standing in his car with its horses slain, the great car-warrior Śrutakarman, sorely enraged, hurled a lance like a great blazing meteor.

sanskrit: sā durmukhasya vipulaṃ varma bhittvā yaśasvinaḥ vidārya prāviśad bhūmiṃ dīpyamānā sutejanā
english: That keen, flaming lance, having cleft through the broad armor of the glorious Durmukha, tore on and entered the earth.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā virathaṃ tatra sutasomo mahābalaḥ paśyatāṃ sarvasainyānāṃ ratham āropayat svakam
english: Seeing him there bereft of his car, the mighty Sutasoma, before the eyes of all the armies, took him up onto his own chariot.

sanskrit: śrutakīrtis tathā vīro jayatsenaṃ sutaṃ tava abhyayāt samare rājan hantukāmo yaśasvinam
english: The hero Śrutakīrti likewise advanced in the battle, O king, against your glorious son Jayatsena, eager to slay him.

sanskrit: tasya vikṣipataś cāpaṃ śrutakīrter mahātmanaḥ ciccheda samare rājañ jayatsenaḥ sutas tava kṣurapreṇa sutīkṣṇena prahasann iva bhārata
english: As high-souled Śrutakīrti drew his bow, your son Jayatsena, O king, cut it asunder in the battle with a keen razor-headed shaft, smiling as it were, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā chinnadhanvānaṃ śatānīkaḥ sahodaram abhyapadyata tejasvī siṃhavad vinadan muhuḥ
english: Seeing his brother with bow cut through, the fiery Śatānīka came to his aid, roaring again and again like a lion.

sanskrit: śatānīkas tu samare dṛḍhaṃ visphārya kārmukam vivyādha daśabhis tūrṇaṃ jayatsenaṃ śilīmukhaiḥ
english: And Śatānīka, twanging his bow hard in the battle, swiftly pierced Jayatsena with ten stone-whetted shafts.

sanskrit: athānyena sutīkṣṇena sarvāvaraṇabhedinā śatānīko jayatsenaṃ vivyādha hṛdaye bhṛśam
english: Then with another keen shaft that cleaves through every armor, Śatānīka pierced Jayatsena deep in the breast.

sanskrit: tathā tasmin vartamāne duṣkarṇo bhrātur antike ciccheda samare cāpaṃ nākuleḥ krodhamūrchitaḥ
english: While this was passing, Duṣkarṇa, beside his brother and mad with rage, severed in the battle the bow of Nakula's son.

sanskrit: athānyad dhanur ādāya bhārasādhanam uttamam samādatta śitān bāṇāñ śatānīko mahābalaḥ
english: Then, taking up another bow, excellent and equal to its burden, the mighty Śatānīka laid hold of sharpened arrows.

sanskrit: tiṣṭha tiṣṭheti cāmantrya duṣkarṇaṃ bhrātur agrataḥ mumoca niśitān bāṇāñ jvalitān pannagān iva
english: And crying "Stand! Stand!" he challenged Duṣkarṇa before his brother and loosed sharp arrows like blazing serpents.

sanskrit: tato 'sya dhanur ekena dvābhyāṃ sūtaṃ ca māriṣa ciccheda samare tūrṇaṃ taṃ ca vivyādha saptabhiḥ
english: Then, O sir, with one shaft he cut his bow and with two his charioteer, swiftly in the battle, and pierced him himself with seven.

sanskrit: aśvān manojavāṃś cāsya kalmāṣān vītakalmaṣaḥ jaghāna niśitais tūrṇaṃ sarvān dvādaśabhiḥ śaraiḥ
english: And that stainless warrior swiftly slew his dappled horses, swift as thought, all of them, with twelve sharp arrows.

sanskrit: athāpareṇa bhallena sumuktena nipātinā duṣkarṇaṃ samare kruddho vivyādha hṛdaye bhṛśam
english: Then with another broad-headed shaft, well-loosed and unerring, the enraged warrior pierced Duṣkarṇa deep in the breast in the battle.

sanskrit: duṣkarṇaṃ nihataṃ dṛṣṭvā pañca rājan mahārathāḥ jighāṃsantaḥ śatānīkaṃ sarvataḥ paryavārayan
english: Seeing Duṣkarṇa slain, O king, five great car-warriors, seeking to kill Śatānīka, surrounded him on every side.

sanskrit: chādyamānaṃ śaravrātaiḥ śatānīkaṃ yaśasvinam abhyadhāvanta saṃrabdhāḥ kekayāḥ pañca sodarāḥ
english: As the glorious Śatānīka was being covered with showers of arrows, the five Kekaya brothers, in fury, rushed to his aid.

sanskrit: tān abhyāpatataḥ prekṣya tava putrā mahārathāḥ pratyudyayur mahārāja gajā iva mahāgajān
english: Seeing them charging on, your sons, great car-warriors, advanced against them, O great king, like elephants against mighty elephants.

sanskrit: durmukho durjayaś caiva tathā durmarṣaṇo yuvā śatruṃjayaḥ śatrusahaḥ sarve kruddhā yaśasvinaḥ pratyudyātā mahārāja kekayān bhrātaraḥ samam
english: Durmukha and Durjaya, the youth Durmarṣaṇa, Śatruṃjaya and Śatrusaha—all those glorious brothers, in fury, advanced together against the Kekayas, O great king.

sanskrit: rathair nagarasaṃkāśair hayair yuktair manojavaiḥ nānāvarṇavicitrābhiḥ patākābhir alaṃkṛtaiḥ
english: With chariots vast as cities, yoked with steeds swift as thought, adorned with banners of varied and brilliant hues,

sanskrit: varacāpadharā vīrā vicitrakavacadhvajāḥ viviśus te paraṃ sainyaṃ siṃhā iva vanād vanam
english: those heroes, bearing splendid bows, with gleaming armor and standards, entered the enemy host as lions pass from forest to forest.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ sutumulaṃ yuddhaṃ vyatiṣaktarathadvipam avartata mahāraudraṃ nighnatām itaretaram anyonyāgaskṛtāṃ rājan yamarāṣṭravivardhanam
english: Then between them, as they smote one another, there raged a tumultuous and most terrible battle, with chariots and elephants locked together—a battle of men who had wronged each other, O king, that swelled the realm of Yama.

sanskrit: muhūrtāstamite sūrye cakrur yuddhaṃ sudāruṇam rathinaḥ sādinaś caiva vyakīryanta sahasraśaḥ
english: After the sun had set a brief while, they waged a most fearful fight; car-warriors and horsemen were strewn about by the thousands.

sanskrit: tataḥ śāṃtanavaḥ kruddhaḥ śaraiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ nāśayām āsa senāṃ vai bhīṣmas teṣāṃ mahātmanām pāñcālānāṃ ca sainyāni śarair ninye yamakṣayam
english: Then the son of Śaṃtanu, Bhīṣma, in fury, with smooth-jointed arrows destroyed the host of those high-souled ones, and with his shafts sent the armies of the Pāñcālas to the abode of Yama.

sanskrit: evaṃ bhittvā maheṣvāsaḥ pāṇḍavānām anīkinīm kṛtvāvahāraṃ sainyānāṃ yayau svaśibiraṃ nṛpa
english: Having thus broken the host of the Pāṇḍavas, that great archer sounded the recall of the armies and withdrew to his own camp, O king.

sanskrit: dharmarājo 'pi saṃprekṣya dhṛṣṭadyumnavṛkodarau mūrdhni caitāv upāghrāya saṃhṛṣṭaḥ śibiraṃ yayau
english: And the King of Righteousness too, beholding Dhṛṣṭadyumna and Vṛkodara, kissed them both upon the head and, well pleased, went to his camp.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca atha śūrā mahārāja parasparakṛtāgasaḥ jagmuḥ svaśibirāṇy eva rudhireṇa samukṣitāḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Then, O great king, the heroes, who had wronged one another, drenched in blood, went each to their own camps.

sanskrit: viśramya ca yathānyāyaṃ pūjayitvā parasparam saṃnaddhāḥ samadṛśyanta bhūyo yuddhacikīrṣayā
english: And having rested as was meet and paid one another due honor, they appeared again in their armor, longing to do battle once more.

sanskrit: tatas tava suto rājaṃś cintayābhipariplutaḥ visravac choṇitāktāṅgaḥ papracchedaṃ pitāmaham
english: Then your son, O king, overwhelmed with care, his limbs smeared with flowing blood, questioned his grandsire thus:

sanskrit: sainyāni raudrāṇi bhayānakāni vyūḍhāni samyag bahuladhvajāni vidārya hatvā ca nipīḍya śūrās te pāṇḍavānāṃ tvaritā rathaughāḥ
english: "The fierce and terrible armies of the Pāṇḍavas, well arrayed and thick with banners—their swift, heroic floods of chariots have torn through, slain, and crushed our hosts.

sanskrit: saṃmohya sarvān yudhi kīrtimanto vyūhaṃ ca taṃ makaraṃ vajrakalpam praviśya bhīmena nibarhito 'smi ghoraiḥ śarair mṛtyudaṇḍaprakāśaiḥ
english: Bewildering all in the fight, those glorious warriors penetrated even that crocodile array, firm as the thunderbolt, and by Bhīma I have been struck down with dreadful arrows that shone like the rod of Death.

sanskrit: kruddhaṃ tam udvīkṣya bhayena rājan saṃmūrchito nālabhaṃ śāntim adya icche prasādāt tava satyasaṃdha prāptuṃ jayaṃ pāṇḍaveyāṃś ca hantum
english: Looking up at him in his wrath, I swooned with terror, O king, and found no peace today. I desire, O you of true vows, by your grace to win victory and to slay the sons of Pāṇḍu."

sanskrit: tenaivam uktaḥ prahasan mahātmā duryodhanaṃ jātamanyuṃ viditvā taṃ pratyuvācāvimanā manasvī gaṅgāsutaḥ śastrabhṛtāṃ variṣṭhaḥ
english: Thus addressed, the high-souled son of Gaṅgā, foremost of those who bear arms, perceiving that Duryodhana was stirred to wrath, smiled, and the wise one, untroubled in mind, answered him:

sanskrit: pareṇa yatnena vigāhya senāṃ sarvātmanāhaṃ tava rājaputra icchāmi dātuṃ vijayaṃ sukhaṃ ca na cātmānaṃ chādaye 'haṃ tvadarthe
english: "Plunging into their host with utmost effort, with my whole soul, O prince, I desire to grant you victory and well-being, nor do I shield myself for your sake.

sanskrit: ete tu raudrā bahavo mahārathā yaśasvinaḥ śūratamāḥ kṛtāstrāḥ ye pāṇḍavānāṃ samare sahāyā jitaklamāḥ krodhaviṣaṃ vamanti
english: But these many fierce car-warriors, glorious, most valiant, masters of weapons, who are the Pāṇḍavas' allies in battle—untiring, they spew forth the venom of their wrath.

sanskrit: te neha śakyāḥ sahasā vijetuṃ vīryonnaddhāḥ kṛtavairās tvayā ca ahaṃ hy etān pratiyotsyāmi rājan sarvātmanā jīvitaṃ tyajya vīra
english: They cannot be conquered here in haste, swollen with valor and made your foes by you. Yet I shall fight against them, O king, with my whole soul, casting away my very life, O hero."
